clue.text: Remain outside a coach, as required by the law

indicators.note: the word for remain sits on the outside, wrapping round the coach

parts.note: to remain is to stay
a coach or private teacher is a tutor

explanation.surface: Someone is told the law obliges them to stay outside a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something statutory is laid down by statute, so it is legally mandatory.

clue.text: I left to start work

indicators.note: the word to is placed at the start, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone departs early so as to begin a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil is hard labour, a synonym for work as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Counters Swiss marksman's hesitations

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head
er is a sound of hesitation, so ers are hesitations

explanation.surface: William Tell falters before taking his famous shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellers count votes or money, so they are people who count.

clue.text: It helps to secure temporary accommodation

definitions.text: It helps to secure temporary accommodation

parts.words: It helps to secure temporary accommodation
parts.note: reads like finding somewhere to stay, but the temporary accommodation is a tent and securing means pinning it to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A peg driven into the ground holds a tent's guy ropes, fastening that portable shelter.

clue.text: Dreary job in which there's nothing worse than defeat

indicators.note: the shorter word is contained within the longer one, so the tail of the job word is cut off

parts.note: routine is a dull repetitive task

explanation.surface: A worker complains that a boring job is the worst setback imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old-style clue: ROUT is the opening of ROUTINE, signalled by 'in which there's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, disorderly defeat, the worst kind of loss.

clue.text: Shocking weather?

parts.note: shocking seems to mean appalling, but literally it means giving electric shocks, as lightning does

explanation.definitionFit: A thunderstorm with lightning is literally full of electrical discharges.

clue.text: Poultry products he'll take to Cockney mate for finest porcelain

parts.note: hens produce eggs
the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters as written
in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, shortened to china

explanation.surface: A man brings eggs to his friend in exchange for fine crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is a London dialect where a word is replaced by a rhyming phrase, often clipped: china (plate) = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell china is very thin translucent porcelain, among the most delicate made.

clue.text: Straight talk from Lombardy?

parts.note: Lombardy in northern Italy is a great flat plain, so its speech might jokingly be the tongue of the plain

explanation.definitionFit: Plain language is clear, direct speech without jargon or evasion.

clue.text: Ale served with roasted apples — fine stuff for knitwear producers

explanation.surface: A pub serves hot ale and apples alongside a knitting supply shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb's wool was an old winter drink of hot spiced ale with roasted apple pulp; it is also soft wool from young sheep used in jumpers.

clue.text: Open manner of early German in front of monster loch

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: the Franks were an early Germanic people
Loch Ness in Scotland is famed for its legendary monster

explanation.surface: An ancient German stands before a Scottish lake with a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness is candour, an openly honest way of speaking.

clue.text: Roguish king breaking into a small church

indicators.note: the king's letter forces its way inside the other pieces

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A villainous monarch burgles a little chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means mischievous or playfully sly, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Looks like the diarist, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is chosen for how it is pronounced when spoken

parts.note: Samuel Pepys was the famous 17th-century English diarist

explanation.surface: Someone resembles the famous diarist, or so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeps are quick glances, so they are brief looks.

clue.text: Ill-fated Russian arts organisation

indicators.note: organising letters arranges them in a new order, so arts is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian arts body comes to a bad end.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Russian emperor, Nicholas II, was murdered with his family in 1918, an ill-fated ruler.

clue.text: Dogfighter

parts.note: suggests an air-combat pilot, but split it reads dog plus fighter, both senses of one word

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a breed of dog and also a pugilist.

clue.text: Plaque left around teeth effectively leads to this sort of denture

indicators.note: the leading letters of the opening words are taken to spell the answer

explanation.surface: A dentist warns that plaque around teeth leads to needing false ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental plate is a set of false teeth mounted on a fitted base.

clue.text: Where in France a Scottish poet outlines a Moslem habit

indicators.note: the poet's name surrounds the other piece like a border

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet
ou is French for where

explanation.surface: A Scottish bard sketches a Muslim custom somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnous is a long hooded cloak worn by Arabs and Berbers, a habit in the sense of garment.

clue.text: Old Spanish craft everybody has gone crazy about

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
gone crazy means the letters of gone are jumbled

parts.note: everybody means all

explanation.surface: Everyone has gone mad over an antique Spanish ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' makes GEON from GONE, and 'about' puts it round ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked sailing warship, used notably by Spain.

clue.text: Small gates made with five pieces of wood

explanation.surface: A carpenter builds little gates from five planks.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's wicket is the target the bowler aims at: three upright stumps with two small bails resting on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small gate; in cricket a wicket is three stumps topped by two bails, five wooden pieces.

clue.text: He may have to wait to give us Malvolio's trade classification

explanation.surface: A servant waits on his master, as Malvolio once did.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward waits on passengers or diners; in Twelfth Night Malvolio is Olivia's steward.

clue.text: Tom and Al acquire an Iberian language

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written, a man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two men named Tom and Al learn a Spanish tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalan is the Romance tongue of Catalonia in north-east Spain, on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: Tidy way to solve a mystery

explanation.surface: A neat way for a detective to crack the case.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up is to put things in order and also to explain or resolve a puzzle.

clue.text: Ring old serving women for breakfast?

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
the ATS (Auxiliary Territorial Service) was the women's branch of the British Army in WWII

explanation.surface: Women from the old army service ring for their morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are eaten as porridge or muesli, a breakfast staple.

clue.text: The home of the brave

parts.note: echoes the American anthem, but the brave is a Native American warrior and this is his dwelling

explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent of skins once lived in by Plains peoples.

clue.text: So it's part of the acanthus genus

indicators.note: the answer forms a part of the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: A botanical note says something belongs to the acanthus genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and so both mean therefore or in this way.

clue.text: A capital solo arrangement

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, so the letters of solo are reordered

explanation.surface: A musician makes a fine arrangement for a solo instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: The jetty I come in through

indicators.note: the letter I enters the middle of the other word

parts.note: per means through or by means of

explanation.surface: Someone arrives by way of the landing stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a structure built out over water, like a jetty.

clue.text: Outdoor type who is devilishly keen on new tunes?

parts.note: fresh means new and air means tune
a fiend is a devil and also an enthusiast or addict

explanation.surface: Someone is wildly enthusiastic about the latest music.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh-air fiend loves being out of doors, a lover of the open air.

clue.text: He doesn't mind losing a sea terminal for freight, apparently

parts.note: goods are freight carried by transport
a port is a harbour where ships load and unload

explanation.surface: A dock for cargo ships is described as unbothered by defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A good sport accepts defeat graciously, a cheerful loser.
